insight: The loader.ts frontmatter parser for persona .md files was extended to handle a nested map-of-arrays (premountedTools) by tracking an inPremountMode state plus currentPremountPlugin. The key insight is that the parser uses indentation to distinguish top-level keys from nested plugin-id keys under premountedTools, and it properly flushes state at boundaries. This pattern generalizes well for future nested YAML structures in persona frontmatter.

When adding a new required method to DronePluginRegistration (like listMountedTools), all mock registration objects in test files must be updated. Using sed to add the property after unmountTool worked but created duplicates when the same line pattern appeared multiple times with different indentation levels. A better approach would be to use a shared helper or spread pattern to construct mock registrations, reducing the number of files needing updates when the interface changes.

When adding a new debug subsystem that must be consumed by the plugin engine (e.g. `--debug tools`), the debug set cannot live privately in the conversation service because the engine is constructed before the conversation service in index.tsx. Extract a shared `DebugFlagRegistry` in drone-core (mirroring `RuntimeFlagRegistry`), created once in index.tsx and passed to both the engine and conversation service. This makes runtime toggling via `/debug` take effect in both layers and makes future debug flags trivial to add.

The drone-agent package resolves drone-core from its built dist/ (package.json "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"), not from source. So after editing drone-core types, you MUST run `pnpm -r run build` before LSP/typecheck in dependent packages reflects the change; otherwise you'll chase stale diagnostics.

conversation-service.ts executes all tool calls in a single assistant turn in parallel via Promise.all (line ~419). Any plugin tool that does read-modify-write on a shared resource (e.g. a JSON file) will race itself when the LLM emits multiple calls to the same target in one turn. Plugin file writers must serialize (in-process per-key mutex) AND use tmp+rename atomic writes, because .drone-agent files aren't always checked into VCS so there's no external safety net. This bit self-improvement (recordInsight/storePrinciple/deletePrinciple); the memory plugin's writeMemoryEntry already used tmp+rename but NOT a mutex.

The project wiki (Obsidian vault at /home/unleet/Obsidian/drone-agent-project) is a separate git repo from the codebase. When ingesting work into the wiki: (1) diff from meta.json's last_commit to HEAD to find new commits; (2) bug fixes with a design choice go in decisions/ as ADRs (per meta/decision-bug-fixes-go-in-decisions.md), not concepts/; (3) update the affected concept/module pages, index.md, log.md, and advance meta.json; (4) commit the wiki repo separately. The .obsidian/workspace.json UI-state churn is tracked and committed alongside wiki content. Completed plans are deleted from project memory and that deletion is committed in the codebase repo.
